question: I'm a software specialist and have worked for a company in China for two years. The company is transferring me to its Stockholm office for one year, and I will remain employed by the company in China during the transfer. What salary do I need for a work permit?
reference_answer: This is a transfer within a company from a company established outside the EEA and Switzerland, of a specialist, for more than 90 days, with at least three months' employment in the company before it: an ICT permit (6 b kap. 1 § utlänningslagen), not an ordinary work permit. Its pay rule is different: the pay must be at least the lowest pay that Swedish collective agreements or practice in the occupation or industry give for full-time work, and not worse than what they require. The 90 percent of the median salary of the ordinary work permit (6 kap. 2 §) is not the test for an ICT permit, and the law gives no amount in kronor for it.
notes: The special kind of permit is described by its facts, not named: an employer outside the EEA, a specialist, a transfer within the company for more than 90 days. The answer must not give the ordinary permit's 90 percent rule as the answer. Reviewed by the maintainer 2026-11-26: the first wording ("my company is transferring me to its Stockholm office") did not establish that the ICT rules apply; the facts were added. Approved as revised. From the probes of 2026-11-26 for rule 5 of the answer prompt; see docs/DESIGN.md.

question: A company established in Sweden has hired me to pick wild berries in the forest this summer. What do I need to get a work permit?
reference_answer: A permit for seasonal work, not an ordinary work permit. Picking wild berries in the forest is excluded from the ordinary work-permit route: a work permit under 6 kap. 2 § första stycket utlänningslagen may not be granted for work as a forest berry picker (utlänningsförordningen 5 kap. 5 §). That is not a bar on every permit: someone with an employment contract for a fixed-term employment as a seasonal worker with an employer established in Sweden is to be granted a permit for seasonal work if the conditions are met (6 c kap. 1 §), and a forest berry picker with such an employer can qualify. The conditions (6 c kap. 2 §) include pay at least equal to the lowest pay under Swedish collective agreements or practice for full-time work, other terms not worse than they require, comprehensive health insurance (held or applied for), and suitable accommodation. The permit is a work permit for seasonal work for a stay of up to 90 days and a residence and work permit for seasonal work for a longer one. An answer that says a forest berry picker cannot get any work permit, or that the seasonal permit is not open to forest berry pickers, is incorrect.
notes: The special kind is described, not named. Guards against reading the exclusion from the ordinary permit (utlänningsförordningen 5 kap. 5 §, checked) as a bar on every permit: on 2026-11-26 an English answer said "as long as you are not picking forest berries" and a Swedish one that forest berry pickers cannot get a work permit. Migrationsverket's English page cites "5 kap 6 §" for the exclusion, its Swedish page "5 kap 5 §"; 6 § is the list of occupations exempt from the salary requirement. Reviewed by the maintainer 2026-11-26: the employer established in Sweden and the forest were added to the question; 6 c kap. 1 § (who the seasonal-work regime is for) and 2 § (the conditions for the permit) are separate required sources, since they establish different things. Approved as revised. From the probes of 2026-11-26 for rule 5 of the answer prompt; see docs/DESIGN.md.

question: What insurance must my employer have for my work permit?
reference_answer: By the time the employment starts, the employer must have taken out health insurance, life insurance, industrial injuries insurance and occupational pension insurance for the employee (Migrationsverket's requirement for an ordinary work permit). In law, the insurance cover, like the pay and other terms, must not be worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the occupation or industry (6 kap. 2 § första stycket utlänningslagen). Separately, for an employment of at most one year the employee must have, or have applied for, a comprehensive health insurance of their own.
notes: A requirement for getting a work permit, no kind named: an answer for the ordinary permit is expected, not a question back. Reviewed by the maintainer 2026-11-26: approved as written. From the probes of 2026-11-26 for rule 5 of the answer prompt; see docs/DESIGN.md.

question: Can I start working while my application for a work permit is being processed?
reference_answer: It depends on facts the question does not give, so the first response should ask: "Is this your first work-permit application or an extension, and do you currently hold a valid permit allowing you to work?" As a general rule a first work permit must be applied for and granted before entry, and an application made after entry is not approved, subject to the exceptions the law lists (6 kap. 4 § utlänningslagen); a person waiting for a first permit may not start working on the strength of the application. Someone who has had a work permit for at least six months and applied for an extension before it expired may keep working while waiting, and may start a new job after applying, sending the new employment contract to Migrationsverket. A valid permit the person already holds may give a right to work of its own, within that permit's restrictions, until it ends. The answer need not cover every branch before asking.
notes: What a person may do, not what is needed to get a permit: still asked back (the limit of the rule 5 default). Close to work-working-while-pending-105, which says "my first application"; this one says nothing about which application it is. Optional supporting source, not required by the retrieval score: 6 kap. 4 § utlänningslagen. Reviewed by the maintainer 2026-11-26: question and kind kept; the reference qualified and the question to ask back made specific. question: Can I change jobs?
reference_answer: It depends on the permit the person holds, so the first response should ask: "What type of residence or work permit do you currently hold?" (not "which work permit", which assumes they have one). With an ordinary work permit it depends on how the permit is restricted (6 kap. 2 a § utlänningslagen): it is tied to a particular employer and a particular kind of work, and after two years of permits in total only to a kind of work. While it is tied to the employer, a new employer needs a new work-permit application; once it is tied only to the kind of work, a new employer in the same occupation does not, but a new occupation always does. When a new application is needed, the person may start the new job after applying if the application was made before the current permit expired, and the new employer must have advertised the position (Migrationsverket's page on changing employer or profession). A person with permanent residence needs no work permit (2 kap. 8 c §), and a residence permit to live with someone in Sweden already carries the right to work; they can change jobs freely.
notes: No permit named at all: the answer must not assume a work permit. Optional supporting sources, not required by the retrieval score: 2 kap. 8 c § utlänningslagen (permanent residence), 6 kap. 2 a § (how a work permit is tied), and Migrationsverket's page for employers on people who already have the right to work in Sweden. Reviewed by the maintainer 2026-11-26: question and kind kept; the reference no longer says that every change of employer needs a new application.
